Chapter 6: Surrendering Control and Embracing Dependence
You know, there comes a moment in almost every life when that sense of control... just slips right through your fingers. Maybe it’s a sudden diagnosis, a relationship you thought would last, or a dream you quietly watched fall apart. The instinct is to fix it—to manage, to force a solution. But as the days go by, it hits you: some things just can’t be forced into place, no matter how hard you try.
Picture a father—someone who’s always been sure he could provide and protect. Now, bills are mounting, his child’s struggling in school, and the future feels more uncertain than ever. He does everything he can to keep it all together, but the weight keeps growing. Then one night, when the house is finally quiet, he sits in the dark and whispers to himself, “I can’t do it all.” It’s terrifying, but there’s also this strange sense of freedom.
In that quiet moment of surrender, something actually changes. He starts to realize that being dependent isn’t a sign of weakness—it’s an entryway to a deeper kind of strength. Letting go of the urge to control every outcome? That takes real courage. It’s not about just giving up or checking out—it’s about trusting that he doesn’t have to carry the load all alone.
For many of us, surrender isn’t just a one-time thing; it’s a rhythm we learn. Every morning brings fresh worries and that old temptation to chase after certainty. But each time you release your grip, you might notice a little more peace, a gentle reminder that life isn’t meant to be managed solo. Dependence—something you might’ve feared—can quietly become your source of confidence.
Now, think about a business owner watching her company slip away. She’s grieving, she’s angry, she’s asking all the hard questions. But as she starts to let go of her plans and expectations, something unexpected happens. Friends show up with meals, a new opportunity appears, and she realizes her worth isn’t measured by her bank account or business card. The journey is still tough, but she’s not carrying it by herself anymore.
Over time, it starts to make sense—surrender isn’t about giving up, it’s about giving over. It’s handing your messy, complicated life into the care of something loving and steady that’s always at work. The freedom you find isn’t about never struggling again. It’s about knowing that, even in the middle of the struggle, there’s real hope.
